## Question 1: Inference about a Population Mean (13 marks)

### Part A: Oyster Shell Height at a New Lease Site

1. **B.** $\mu$ is the population mean shell height of all market-size oysters at the new lease site. $79.2$ mm is the sample mean (a statistic), and $76$ mm is the null value.
2. **D.** Hypotheses are about the parameter $\mu$, and the grower asks whether the mean is *greater than* $76$ mm:
$$H_0:\mu=76\qquad H_a:\mu>76$$
3. **A.**
$$SE=\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}=\frac{6.4}{\sqrt{16}}=\frac{6.4}{4}=1.600\text{ mm}$$
Option B divides by $n$, option C divides by $\sqrt{n-1}$, and option D is $s$ itself.
4. **C.**
$$t=\frac{79.2-76}{1.600}=\frac{3.2}{1.600}=2.000$$
$$df=n-1=16-1=15$$
5. **B.** In the $df=15$ row,
$$1.753<2.000<2.131$$
which correspond to upper-tail probabilities $0.050$ and $0.025$. The alternative is upper-tailed, so
$$0.025<P\text{-value}<0.050$$
(The exact P-value is about $0.032$.)
6. **A.** Because $P<0.05$, reject $H_0$. The conclusion is about the population mean, not the sample mean (D), and a test never proves an exact value (C).
7. **D.** A two-sided test doubles the one-tail area:
$$2(0.025)<P\text{-value}<2(0.050)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 0.050<P\text{-value}<0.100$$
Since $P>0.05$, fail to reject $H_0$. This is why the alternative must be chosen before seeing the data.

### Part B: Resting Heart Rate of Racehorses

8. **C.** Each horse is measured twice, so the before and after values are linked. The analysis uses one sample of $12$ differences, with $df=12-1=11$ (the number of pairs minus one).
9. **A.** With $d=\text{after}-\text{before}$, a lower heart rate after the program gives a negative $d$:
$$H_0:\mu_d=0\qquad H_a:\mu_d<0$$
10. **D.**
$$SE_{\bar{d}}=\frac{s_d}{\sqrt{n}}=\frac{4.2}{\sqrt{12}}=1.212$$
$$t=\frac{\bar{d}-0}{SE_{\bar{d}}}=\frac{-3.5}{1.212}=-2.887$$
11. **B.** By symmetry, use $|t|=2.887$ in the $df=11$ row:
$$2.718<2.887<3.106$$
which correspond to upper-tail probabilities $0.010$ and $0.005$. The alternative is lower-tailed (one tail), so
$$0.005<P\text{-value}<0.010$$
Option C is the two-sided range. (The exact P-value is about $0.0074$.) Since $P<0.05$, the trainer would reject $H_0$.
12. **C.**
$$m=t^*\,SE_{\bar{d}}=2.201(1.212)=2.669$$
$$\bar{d}\pm m=-3.5\pm2.669\quad\Longrightarrow\quad(-6.169,\ -0.831)$$
Option A uses $z^*=1.960$, option B uses $s_d$ instead of the standard error, and option D has the wrong sign.
13. **A.** Reversing the subtraction flips the sign of every difference, so $\bar{d}=3.5$ and $t=2.887$. A reduction in heart rate now gives a positive difference, so $H_a:\mu_d>0$. The standard error, degrees of freedom, P-value and conclusion are unchanged.


## Question 2: Nitrate in PEI Private Wells (7 marks)

1. **D.** $p$ is the proportion of all private wells in PEI with nitrate above the guideline this year. $0.25$ is the sample proportion and $0.20$ is the null value.
2. **B.** The agency asks whether the proportion has *changed*, in either direction:
$$H_0:p=0.20\qquad H_a:p\neq0.20$$
3. **C.** The test uses expected counts under $H_0$:
$$np_0=400(0.20)=80\ge10\qquad n(1-p_0)=400(0.80)=320\ge10$$
Option A is the condition for the confidence interval (observed counts), not the test.
4. **A.**
$$\hat{p}=\frac{100}{400}=0.250$$
The null standard error uses $p_0$, not $\hat{p}$:
$$SE_0=\sqrt{\frac{(0.20)(0.80)}{400}}=\sqrt{0.0004}=0.020$$
$$z=\frac{0.250-0.20}{0.020}=2.500$$
Option B wrongly uses $\hat{p}$ in the test's standard error.
5. **D.** In the $df=\infty$ row,
$$2.326<2.500<2.576$$
which correspond to upper-tail probabilities $0.010$ and $0.005$. Doubling for the two-sided alternative,
$$0.010<P\text{-value}<0.020$$
Since $P<0.05$, reject $H_0$. (The exact P-value is about $0.0124$.)
6. **B.** The interval uses $\hat{p}$ in the standard error:
$$SE=\sqrt{\frac{(0.25)(0.75)}{400}}=0.02165$$
$$m=1.960(0.02165)=0.04243$$
$$0.250\pm0.04243\quad\Longrightarrow\quad(0.208,\ 0.292)$$
The observed counts $X=100\ge15$ and $n-X=300\ge15$ support the large-sample interval. Option A wrongly uses $SE_0$, option C is centred at $p_0$, and option D uses $z^*=1.645$.
7. **C.** The confidence level describes the long-run success rate of the method, not a probability for one interval (A), and the interval estimates a population proportion, not a range for individual wells (B). The interval excludes $0.20$, which agrees with rejecting $H_0$ at $\alpha=0.05$.
